title: Aurum Cortex — Search Ranking Tuning (Hosted API walkthrough)
summary: Walkthrough of Redwood hosted embeddings + reranking endpoints for Aurum Cortex. Covered integration patterns for their product search, tuning strategies (hybrid sparse + semantic, reranker stack), Console walkthrough for model selection, Optimize suggestions for batching and quantization, and security/compliance notes. Agreed next steps: pilot dataset upload, pricing estimate, and a follow-up bench run with 100k queries.
next_steps: Samir to send pilot pricing and SLO options
Devon to share sample dataset + 2 week traffic profile
action_items: Samir: send pilot pricing + quickstart links (due 2028-06-16)
Jules: prepare benchmark run template and request for tokens (due 2028-06-21)
Devon: upload sample 100k query set to shared S3 link (due 2028-06-20)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes, is that still good?
[00:05] Maya (Aurum): Yep that works, Samir, thanks — we've got Dev and Priya on.
[00:12] Jules (Redwood SE): Hi all, quick intros: I run the inference perf stuff, I’ll demo the hosted embeddings + the reranker flow and then we can dig into cost/latency tradeoffs.
[00:22] Devon (Aurum): Quick context — our product search is a mix of BM25 + embeddings for long-tail queries. We're seeing hit rate issues and re-ranking is slow at peak.
[00:30] Maya: Key success metric is increasing top-3 MRR by 12% without doubling token cost or adding >40ms median latency.
[00:42] Samir: Perfect, we'll keep that goal in mind. Jules, want to start the console demo?
[00:47] Jules: Sure. I'm going to share my screen — there might be a slight delay. (screen share noise) OK, console home, model catalog. For hosted embeddings we recommend a dense vector model optimized in our catalog — we show measured recall and token cost per 1k vectors here, note that these are measured on typical 128-d sequence workloads.
[01:15] Devon: Those numbers look good. How do you handle dimension mismatch? Our existing vectors are 768-d.
[01:22] Jules: Good call — Redwood supports model variants and conversions in the pipeline, but for hosted we'll often run a small conversion job or use a compatible model. For reranker we accept the original query+doc pair as inputs to the reranker API — that model handles cross-encodes at 768 dims, you don't need to pre-embed the doc.
[01:40] Maya: So we could keep our current offline embed pipeline for the index and call Redwood embeddings for live queries?
[01:47] Jules: Exactly. Typical pattern: index with your precomputed vectors; use Redwood embeddings for online query vectors, then dense retrieval + optional sparse signals, and send top-N to the reranker. The reranker is a hosted endpoint that streams a score for each candidate.
[02:05] Devon: Latency — if we're talking top-10 rerank, what median latencies are you seeing?
[02:12] Jules: For our verified profiles, a mid-sized reranker on GPU with batching turned off for strict latency gets ~45–60ms median per request with 10 candidates. If you allow micro-batching up to 8 we can push cost down to the low 30s but tail may move a bit.
[02:30] Maya: Tail is important for us — checkout flows can't be slow.
[02:34] Samir: We can configure per-route SLOs and automatic fallback: if a reranker tail breaches threshold, traffic routes to a cheaper cross-encoder variant or a dense-only heuristic.
[02:46] Devon: How does that fallback look in practice? Do you keep cached scores?
[02:51] Jules: Yes — Redwood maintains a prefix/KV cache so if you re-rank a known candidate set, we serve from cache. Cache keys are request-hashable; TTLs are configurable per customer. Sometimes people call it KV cash in notes; we've seen transcriptions say "KV cash" so just flag that.
[03:10] Priya (Aurum): Security — our compliance team will ask about SSO, audit logs, and data residency. Do you have SOC 2 reports?
[03:18] Samir: We do — SOC 2 Type II, ISO efforts in progress. For hosted we provide detailed audit logs and can push logs to your SIEM. For sensitive PII you can opt for Private deployment or VPC peering.
[03:33] Maya: VPC peering — does hosted support customer-managed VPC?
[03:36] Jules: Hosted supports VPC peering for Dedicated mode; for pure hosted we have region controls and encryption at rest. If you need full network isolation we usually propose Redwood Private.
[03:48] Devon: OK. For cost: how do tokens + embeddings get charged?
[03:52] Samir: Embeddings are billed per vector request and per 1k tokens for generative rerankers when applicable. Our pricing page shows per-embedding unit and per-token for rerank models; for pilots we often do a blended pilot estimate. I'll send a sheet.
[04:06] Maya: Would be helpful to see a blended example with 100k queries/day and top-10 rerank.
[04:11] Samir: We'll include that in the pricing doc.
[04:15] Jules: Back to the demo — switching to the API playground. Here's an example call for the embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, payload is query text. Response includes vector and cost meta. For reranker: POST /v1/rerank with items array of candidate docs and the query, returns ranked items and per-item scores.
[04:39] Devon: How does streaming work? Can rerank stream incremental scores?
[04:43] Jules: Reranker streams the overall score, not token streams like generation. We optimize the scorer path to be low-latency and can stream partial buckets for very large lists.
[04:52] Maya: What about batching and KV cache settings for our traffic shape — we have spiky traffic around midnights and promotions.
[05:00] Jules: Redwood Optimize analyzes traffic and suggests batching thresholds. For spiky workloads we recommend adaptive batching with a small max latency budget (e.g., 30ms). We also suggest prefix caching of frequently seen queries. In Console you'll see suggestions like "batch target 8, max latency 30ms, enable prefix cache TTL 12h".
[05:21] Devon: Any quantization recommendations? We are sensitive to slight quality regressions.
[05:25] Jules: For production, 4-bit quant with QAT is common for embeddings; rerankers tolerate 8-bit in some cases. Our Optimize tool will run a small A/B against your eval set to quantify deltas before recommending.
[05:38] Priya: That eval — do you run it on our data? Is it persisted?
[05:42] Samir: It's ephemeral for the eval unless you opt-in to retain results. For pilots we recommend sharing a small labeled set — we'll run the eval in our test environment and share metrics.
[05:53] Maya: Ok, show me the console rollout UI.
[05:56] Jules: Rollouts: you can canary to X% traffic, set automatic rollback if MRR drops or latency increases beyond thresholds. You can pin a model for a route and create a fallback chain — hosted->dedicated->private variants.
[06:12] Devon: Is there any way to do local A/B for just desktop users?
[06:15] Jules: Yes, route keys support user segmentation — you can tie a cookie or user_id hash to a traffic split.
[06:21] Maya: Any gotchas in integration? We use a serverless front end with lambda edge.
[06:26] Jules: Watch for cold-starts if you're calling reranker from a Lambda per-request. We recommend a thin aggregator service to batch queries, or using Redwood's SDK with a persistent connection. Also set client-side timeouts slightly above the route SLO.
[06:40] Devon: For the bench run, what telemetry will you collect?
[06:44] Jules: We'll collect per-request latency percentiles, token counts, model throughput, cache hit rates, and cost per 1k. We'll share a workbook with those metrics and the raw traces for 7-day windows.
[06:56] Maya: Sounds good. Any competitor differences we should be mindful of?
[07:00] Samir: Compared to OpenAI-like hosted models, Redwood exposes deployment controls (rollouts, private variants) and cost levers (batching, cache) in a single pane; Vertex has tight cloud integration but less opinionated reranker tooling. Anthropic's safety and model family differences came up earlier.
[07:20] Priya: Ok, last: timelines. We want to pilot before end of July.
[07:24] Samir: That's doable. Plan: you send sample data by 6/20, we scope pricing and pilot by 6/16, SE bench run week of 6/27, pilot 3–4 weeks after bench depending on results.
[07:40] Maya: Great.
[07:42] Samir: Quick recap of next steps... (recap follows)
[07:48] Devon: One more question — are there prebuilt connectors for our search infra? We run Elasticsearch with a custom scoring plugin.
[07:54] Jules: We have connectors and a small adapter library for ES that handles vector joins and rerank insertions. We'll share that repo link.
[08:04] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[08:06] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up with the pricing doc and the bench run template.
[08:10] (call ends)

Note: transcription has a few mis-hearings and simplified technical terms; timestamps roughly every 20-80 seconds.
